text:
alex: Heads-up — mobile clients are hitting reconnects a lot and our token accounting looks off when they resume streaming. Seeing duplicate partial token charges sometimes. :thinking:

mira: any reproducible trace or client logs? which header are they sending for resume?

alex: I have one trace, attaching inline. client sent `Resume-Token: qJ39...` then disconnected, reconnected after 6s and server charged ~1.8x tokens for the same last chunk.

devon: could be our double-count on resumed chunks — we currently apply the partial-token delta on reconnect and also replay buffered tokens from the pre-close window.

sam: is the policy per-org or per-key for burst credits? If per-org, a reconnect may consume org-level burst twice if we mishandle the resume.

alex: for this customer it's per-key, but we do both per-key and per-org throttles, yes.

leo: quick idea: assign ephemeral stream-credit-id on start and mark it consumed on finalization. On reconnect, server checks if stream-credit-id was already finalized; if so, only apply incremental. That avoids duplicate.

mira: I like that, but it requires storing short-lived state for every open stream. Concern: heavy memory pressure at scale — thousands of idle but resumable streams.

sam: can we instead make the resume token idempotent? e.g. resume token includes `stream_epoch` and `last_ack_offset`, and we store a tiny tombstone for N seconds. Tombstone TTL could be equal to max client reconnect window (30s).

alex: tombstone route seems less memory-intensive than full session state. But we still need metrics to detect when tokens were double-charged.

quota-bot: [automated] Alert: spike in "stream_resume_double_charge" for org: acme-inc by 12x in the last 10m.

mira: metrics we should surface on Console: per-key burst_credits, in-flight resumable_streams, resume_failures, double_charge_events. That helps support quickly correlate.

leo: UX idea: Console shows live "burst window" indicator + estimated remaining burst credits and last refill time; helpful for customer visibility and debugging.

devon: implementation detail debate: do we apply burst credits at token emission time or at chunk commit? Current behavior: on chunk send we decrement credits immediately. If we keep that, reconnect replay can re-send chunk without server knowing it was previously charged.

sam: suggestion: use two-phase commit for chunks: reserve on send, finalize on ack. Reserve reduces available credits but doesn't finalize billing until ack or stream close. If reconnect repeats send, server can match by sequence id and ignore duplicates during finalize.

alex: two-phase would fix correctness, but increases complexity and state. We need to estimate extra memory and latency. Also edge cases: client crash and never ack -> reservation leak. TTLs again.

mira: TTL-based cleanup possible; reserve expires after N seconds and credit is refunded. We should pick conservative TTL = max expected network jitter + reconnect window (~60s).

devon: also need to consider rate-limit headers we expose: `X-RW-Burst-Remaining`, `X-RW-Resume-Window`, `X-RW-Stream-Reserved`. Clients rely on these to decide backoff. If we change semantics, update SDKs.

leo: about backoff: clients currently try exponential backoff but immediate reconnects (0-3s) are common. We might implement server-side soft-deny with `Retry-After` and a separate `Retry-After-Resume` for resumable streams to steer clients.

sam: Can we implement a quick fix for this week's incident? Proposal: tombstone resume tokens for 45s and emit a metric whenever a resume tries to re-finalize the same chunk; then roll out two-phase in Q2 as planned.

mira: +1 for quick fix. Also add a temporary alert for resume double charge > 3 events/min per-org.

alex: I'll prototype tombstone store (redis with small keys) and metrics. Who can help test?

devon: I can wire the metric and the rate-limit headers. Will add `X-RW-Resume-Status: resumed|already-finalized|new` for debugging.

leo: I'll update Console mockups for burst and resume panels so Support can flip on the toggle.

quota-bot: [automated] Runbook suggestion: If double-charge alert fires, flip `stream_resume_tombstone_ttl` to 60s, and enable `console.resume_debug` for affected orgs.

alex: pairing session 11:00 PT tomorrow to demo trace and deploy tombstone behind a feature flag. I'll drop PR later today.

mira: also let's craft a canary: route 1% of streaming traffic for a few orgs to the tombstone handler, monitor `stream_resume_double_charge` and `stream_resume_latency`. If no regressions, scale to 20%.

sam: and add a fallback: if tombstone store becomes overloaded, servers should fall back to rejecting resumes with `409 Resume Not Supported` instead of silently double-charging. That keeps correctness even under partial outage.

alex: noted. thanks everyone. I'll post PR link here when ready. :thumbsup:
